subject.title: enhancement: Optimize voice message processing pipeline for Telegram

question: What Telegram voice pipeline contract should OpenClaw support before implementation: narrow feedback improvements, async/background TTS delivery, a priority voice lane, or a full staged STT/TTS pipeline with state snapshots?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the requested fix spans Telegram ingress ordering, STT provider behavior, TTS delivery semantics, caching policy, and session-state visibility, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Design measured staged pipeline
options.body: Keep this as the broad tracker, use narrower issues for typing and delivery-mode slices, and require live benchmarks plus state snapshots before coding the async STT/TTS pipeline.

options.title: Limit scope to near-term UX
options.body: Treat the typing-cue and separate text-plus-voice delivery issues as the immediate work while leaving priority queues, streaming, and caching unplanned for now.

options.title: Defer broad pipeline work
options.body: Keep current provider tuning and delivery semantics until stronger live evidence shows a staged voice pipeline is worth the complexity.

recommendation.title: Design measured staged pipeline
recommendation.body: Keep this as the broad tracker, use narrower issues for typing and delivery-mode slices, and require live benchmarks plus state snapshots before coding the async STT/TTS pipeline.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans TTS core behavior, Telegram delivery policy, and product-level async semantics, and the strongest combined history points to this owner candidate.
